title: SLA-weighted Preemptive Admission with Burst Buffers for Dedicated Fleets
creator: Marco Li
description:
Problem: Dedicated fleets sometimes see short bursts of high concurrency from customers with mixed SLA tiers. Current admission shapers are either global (coarse) or fair-queue-based and do not allow preemption of low-priority queued requests when high-priority traffic arrives. This causes SLA violations for committed customers and inefficient use of reserved headroom.

Goal: Implement a SLA-weighted Preemptive Admission (SWPA) subsystem with an in-memory per-fleet burst buffer that preserves short bursts for high-SLA traffic, preemptively evicts lower-weight queued requests when necessary, and exposes tunable knobs for weight policies, soft-deadlines, and burst budget accounting. This should integrate with autoscaling headroom signals so admission reacts to both transient and persistent capacity shifts.
design:
Core components:
1) Burst Buffer: a bounded, memory-backed queue per fleet that holds admitted-but-not-yet-dispatched requests. Size is expressed in 'request tokens' and configurable per-fleet.
2) Scoreboard + Token-Bucket: Each incoming request is assigned an SLA weight; admission consumes tokens from a fast token-bucket reservoir (short-term throughput budget). When the reservoir is exhausted, requests are placed into the burst buffer if space remains.
3) Preemptive Eviction: When a high-weight request arrives and buffer is full, the scoreboard finds candidate queued requests with lower effective SLA weight and evicts them (eviction order: lowest weight, longest queued). Evicted requests get explicit response codes and metrics.
4) Soft Deadlines: Each queued request carries a soft deadline (ms) after which it is eligible for shedding even if its weight would otherwise protect it. Deadlines avoid indefinite queuing for long requests.
5) Predictive Headroom Estimator (PHE): Monitors real-time telemetry (avg seq length, token gen rate, KV cache hit ratio) and outputs a headroom factor that dynamically scales the admission token rate. PHE uses exponential smoothing and a conservative bias to avoid oscillation.
6) Policy Engine: Fleet-level config that maps customer SLA tier -> weight, burst budget, soft-deadline, min-guarantee tokens, and preemption enabled flag.

Data structures: lightweight concurrent priority lists keyed by (weight, enqueue_time) with O(log n) eviction lookup. Admission path must be bounded in 99.9th percentile decision latency (<200us) to keep tail response behavior predictable.
config_schema:
New fleet config fields (yaml/json):
- admission:
  - enabled: boolean
  - token_bucket_capacity: integer (tokens)
  - token_refill_rate: float (tokens/sec)
  - burst_buffer_size: integer (tokens)
  - sla_weights: map<string,int> (e.g., 'gold':100,'silver':50,'bronze':10)
  - soft_deadline_ms: integer
  - preemptive_eviction: boolean
  - min_guarantee_tokens_per_sla: map<string,int>
  - predictive_headroom_enabled: boolean
  - predictive_headroom_params: map<string,string> (tunable EMA windows)

Config must validate that burst_buffer_size >= max(requests per second * expected short burst ms / average token cost).
api_changes:
Server-side only. No public REST change for customers initially. Internal APIs:
- /fleet/<id>/admission/config (GET/PUT) for operators to tune policy.
- telemetry endpoints: /fleet/<id>/admission/metrics for debug export.
- admission decision trace: per-request trace tag 'admission_debug' emitted when debugging enabled.

Future: expose per-customer SLA hints in runtime headers to allow proactive client-side retry/backoff guidance.
telemetry:
Metrics to add:
- admission.tokens.available (gauge)
- admission.tokens.refill_rate (gauge)
- admission.burst_buffer.used (gauge, tokens)
- admission.enqueue.count (counter, by sla)
- admission.evict.count (counter, by sla_evicted, sla_evicted_by)
- admission.drop.count (counter, reason: preempt, soft_deadline)
- admission.queue_wait_ms.p50/p95/p99 (histogram by sla)
- admission.preempt.latency (histogram)
- admission.headroom.factor (gauge from PHE)

Logs: structured event on eviction with fields (fleet, evicted_sla, evicted_request_id, cause, current_headroom).
Dashboards: per-fleet SLA health panel showing queued counts, eviction rate, and predicted headroom. Alerts: eviction_rate > threshold and p99 queue wait > SLA configured limit -> paging.
rollout_plan:
1) Feature flag gated in runtime (disabled by default).
2) Canary: enable on a low-traffic dedicated fleet (dev/dogfood) for 72 hours with telemetry enabled. Validate decision latency and eviction rates.
3) Limited beta: allow opt-in fleets via API toggle for customers with mixed SLAs. Monitor errors and headroom impact for 2 weeks.
4) Gradual ramp: enable for 20% of fleets, then 50%, then 100% with automated rollback if eviction_rate spikes or p99 latency regresses.
5) Post-rollout: iterate on PHE parameters and add sibling autoscaler integration to coordinate token refill_rate with scale-up events.
test_plan:
Unit tests: token bucket refill, eviction correctness, soft-deadline expiry.
Load tests: synthetic mixed-SLA workload with random burst patterns to verify that gold SLA p95 latency meets target while bronze may be shed. Use k6 + local runtime harness.
Chaos tests: simulate delayed autoscaler and ensure admission doesn't deadlock or accept requests beyond min-guarantee.
Integration tests: end-to-end on staging with canary fleet, assert metrics exported and no regression on tail latency.
Performance: microbench admission path to ensure decision <200us at 95th and minimal allocation pressure.
acceptance_criteria: Gold SLA p95 latency on canary fleet does not increase by more than 10% under test bursts compared to baseline without SWPA
Preemptive evictions are correctly attributed and produce consistent telemetry (evicted_sla, by_sla) in >=95% of simulated scenarios
Admission decision median latency <50us, p95 <200us in stress tests
Predictive Headroom Estimator provides stable headroom factor (no oscillation) across 30m windows in CI load generator
Feature flag can be toggled per-fleet without restarting runtime and toggling produces no request loss beyond intended preemptions
tasks: Implement burst buffer data structure and eviction scoreboard (ENG)
Add token-bucket reservoir and fast admission path (ENG)
Implement Predictive Headroom Estimator and config knobs (ENG)
End-to-end load tests and perf benchmarking (SRE)
Documentation: runbook, config guide, and public beta notes (Docs/PM)
notes: Trade-offs: preemptive eviction favors committed-paying customers but increases user-visible errors for shed tenants; documentation and retry guidance are required.
We intentionally keep decision path lock-light and in-process to hit microsecond latencies; persistent queues (kafka/redis) are out-of-scope for this phase.

Autoscaler integration is planned: token_refill_rate should be a leaky bucket tied to desired throughput; when a scale-up is in progress, PHE should conservatively reduce refill rate to avoid oscillation.

Security: admission subsystem does not persist customer payloads; eviction events log request ids and SLA only. If future requirements need payload persistence for debugging, consult security for retention policy.
